### Figure 4 - James
```{r figure-4}
data_4 <- data %>%
  ## Convert Flourishing Scale scores from string into numeric values ##
  mutate(
    pre_fs_scale = as.numeric(pre_fs_scale),
    post_fs_score = as.numeric(post_fs_score),
    postnatal_florishing_scale_score = as.numeric(postnatal_florishing_scale_score)
    ) %>%
  ## Remove missing values, if not done, the calculated means will be wrong ##
  filter(
    !is.na(pre_fs_scale),
    !is.na(post_fs_score),
    !is.na(postnatal_florishing_scale_score)
    ) %>%
  ## Calculate means and standard deviations for each of the 3 time points ##
  group_by(intervention_group) %>%
  summarise(
    pre_mean = mean(pre_fs_scale),
    pre_sd = sd(pre_fs_scale),
    post_mean = mean(post_fs_score),
    post_sd = sd(post_fs_score),
    postnatal_mean = mean(postnatal_florishing_scale_score),
    postnatal_sd = sd(postnatal_florishing_scale_score)
    )

## Pivot the data so that the 3 time points can be plotted and labelled on the x-axis with standard deviations and means
data_4_long <- data_4 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pre_mean, post_mean, postnatal_mean),
    names_to = "timepoint",
    values_to = "mean" # The pivot is only done to the means, the standard deviation can later be added manually.
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    sd = case_when(
      timepoint == "pre_mean" ~ pre_sd,
      timepoint == "post_mean" ~ post_sd,
      timepoint == "postnatal_mean" ~ postnatal_sd # Adds in the standard deviation for each time point manually
      ),
    timepoint = factor( 
      timepoint, 
      levels = c("pre_mean", "post_mean", "postnatal_mean"),
      labels = c("Before the intervention\n(II trimester of pregnancy)",
                 "After the intervention\n(III trimester of pregnancy)",
                 "Follow-up\n(± 5 months postpartum)" # Adds labels for each time point
                 )
      ),
    intervention_group = factor(intervention_group) # Makes intervention_group be treated as categorical
    )

## Plot the graph
ggplot(data_4_long, aes(x = timepoint, y = mean, group = intervention_group, linetype = factor(intervention_group))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd), width = 0.03, linetype = "solid") + # Creates error bars of the standard deviations
  ## 'M =' text on the graph is added ## 
  geom_text(aes(
    label = sprintf("M = %.2f", mean), # Adds 2 decimal points
    hjust = case_when(
    ## Shifts the first 2 'M = ' text labels to the left of the error bars, and the final one to the right
    grepl("Before|After", timepoint) ~ 1.2,
    grepl("Follow", timepoint) ~ -0.2
    ),
    ## Shifts the 'M = ' up and down as not to overlap with the line.
    vjust = case_when(
      grepl("Before", timepoint) ~ ifelse(intervention_group == 1, 1.3, 0.1), 
      grepl("After", timepoint) ~ ifelse(intervention_group == 1, -1.2, 1.8),
      grepl("Follow", timepoint) ~ ifelse(intervention_group == 1, 0.6, 0.6),
      )
    ),
    size = 3 # Set size of font
    ) +
  ## Legend configuration ##
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") + # Moves legend to the bottom
  guides(linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) + # Stacks the legend guide for the lines
  scale_y_continuous(
    ## Y-axis configuration ##
    limits = c(40, 60), # Sets y-axis from 40 to 60 
    breaks = seq(40, 60, by = 2), # Adds ticks every 2 units
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x) # Adds .00 to the y-axis
    ) +
  ## Line labelling ##
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("1" = "solid", "2" = "dotted"),
    labels = c("HIIT - High Intensity Interval Training Group", "EDU - Educational Intervention Group")
    ) + 
  ## Y-axis is labelled, however I have used the x label in order for it to be at the bottom. ##
  labs(
    x = "**Psychological well-being** (*measured with the Flourishing Scale*)",
    y = NULL,
    linetype = NULL
    ) +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_markdown(margin = margin(t = 15)), # Spaces the y-axis label to be more central
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA), # Makes the legend icon for the lines' background transparent
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1), # Adds the black border around teh graph
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA), # Makes background white
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80", linetype), # Adds the major y-axis grid lines
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank() # Shouldn't be necessary, but I notice that there is a small vertical white line which interrupts the major y-axis grid lines without this.
    )
```

```{r figure-4 improved}
## Plot the graph
ggplot(data_4_long, aes(x = timepoint, y = mean, group = intervention_group, color = factor(intervention_group))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  # Creates error bars of the standard deviations
  ## 'M =' text on the graph is added ## 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd), width = 0.06, linetype = "solid", position = position_dodge(width = 0.03)) + # Error bars are shifted horizontally so no longer overlap
  geom_text(aes(
    label = sprintf("M = %.2f", mean), # Adds 2 decimal points to the 'M = '
    hjust = case_when(
    ## Shifts the first 2 'M = ' text labels to the left of the error bars, and the final one to the right
      grepl("Before|After", timepoint) ~ 1.2,
      grepl("Follow", timepoint) ~ -0.2
      ),
  vjust = case_when(
    ## Shifts the 'M = ' up and down as not to overlap with the line.
    grepl("Before", timepoint) ~ ifelse(intervention_group == 1, 1.3, 0.1),
    grepl("After", timepoint) ~ ifelse(intervention_group == 1, -1.2, 1.8),
    grepl("Follow", timepoint) ~ ifelse(intervention_group == 1, 0.6, 0.6)
    )
  ),
  size = 3.2, # Change size of 'M = ' text
  fontface = "bold", # Makes it bold
  show.legend = FALSE # Otherwise there will be an 'a' in the legend key overlapping with the line
  ) +
  ## Legend configuration ##
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") + # Moves legend to the bottom
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) + # Stacks the legend guide for the lines
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(40, 56), # Sets y-axis from 40 to 60
    breaks = seq(40, 60, by = 2) # Sets ticks every 2 units
    ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("1" = "dodgerblue", "2" = "brown1"), # Sets contrasting colours for the lines
    labels = c("**HIIT** - High Intensity Interval Training Group", "**EDU** - Educational Intervention Group")
    ) + 
  ## Y-axis is labelled on y-axis, and legend is labelled.
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "**Psychological well-being** (*measured with the Flourishing Scale*)",
    color = "**Intervention Group** (*M = Mean*)"
    ) +
  theme(
    ## element_markdown() is used on several areas of the graph in order to make text bold using the ggtext package.
    axis.title.y = element_markdown(size = 10, margin = margin(t = 15, l = 10, r = 10)), # Y-axis is given margins to better fit onto graph.
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.text = element_markdown(),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA), # Makes lines' key background transparent
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1), # Adds border around the graph
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA), # Makes graph background white
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80"), # Adds major y-axis grid
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(color = "grey80"), # Adds minor y-axis grid
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank() # There is a small vertical white line which interrupts the major y-axis grid lines without this.
    )
```

Contrasting colours are used which makes the trend clear when one line overtakes the other, where before it was difficult to tell. Dotted line is now unnecessary and removed. Error bars shifted horizontally so no longer overlap. Decimals on y-axis removed, it’s just extra cluster. Moving y-axis label to y-axis for less cluster on bottom. Label for the legend with explanation for what M = means added. Added grid minor y so that error bars can be more accurately estimated. Made ‘M =’ bold so easily readable. Y-axis set to 56 to 40 so lines less compressed. Points are added for better visibility.
